before_times: What the errand is: groceries, a pick-up, a return, a drop-off, waiting at the home or a home check
Where it starts and ends (the town or ZIP), and how many stops
Any time it must be done by (a store closing, a return deadline, a delivery window)
How long to book, and for a purchase, the most the customer will OK without a text
after_time: The list, the store, or the item, and what to do if something is out of stock (skip it, or pick the closest match)
Who is at home, and where to leave things
For waiting at the home: the company coming and its window
secure_page_only: The street address and how to get in: a key hand-over, a lockbox code or a garage code (alarm codes are given only to the owner by phone, never typed)
A signed key release: who may hold the key, where it is kept (coded, never with the address), and that it comes back when the errands end
For a pharmacy pick-up: the paper the pharmacy needs, who may sign for it, and the medicine names
The spending limit for each errand, and the card for purchases
intake_questions.who_may_book: An adult for themself. A family member for an older parent, with the parent's OK where they can give it. The person whose home it is OKs any key hand-over. A business books office errands. Nobody under 18 books.

stop: someone hurt or ill right now
someone at home not answering who may need help
go_on: An older adult at home alone: the booking goes on; the concierge checks in with the family contact named on the page.
A dog or other animal at home: the booking goes on; the customer says where it will be. Staff don't walk or feed animals unless the errand says so.
Alcohol or tobacco on a list: bought only where the state's rules let a third party do it, handed only to the customer or a named adult of age, with ID, never left at the door.
A prescription pick-up: only with the paper the pharmacy needs, handed only to the customer or their named adult, never left at the door if it needs a signature or must stay cold.
stop_action: Someone hurt, a fire, a gas smell or a break-in in progress: 'Call 911 now.' No booking until they're safe.
Suicide or self-harm: 'Call or text 988 now; call 911 if anyone is in danger right now.' No booking in that chat; the owner is told, never the words.
A concierge who finds a door open, a window broken or a leak at a home check: photos of the home only, the customer told at once. A break-in found: the concierge leaves and calls 911 first.

Someone at home who doesn't answer and may need help: the concierge calls the customer's contact, then the owner decides about a welfare check. The concierge never calls 911 for the company; the owner does.

prep: Leave the list and any return items and receipts by the door
Put the dry cleaning out, and tell us where pets will be
Send your list by the night before

skills: Errands in a car, with an insured vehicle and a checked driver's license
Waiting at a home for a repair or delivery
Home checks with a photo report
Handling keys (key release and coded storage)
staff.licenses_or_certificates: No person license. Drivers keep a valid driver's license and a clean driving record (the business's rule). Staff who hold keys pass the business's background check.
staff.who_oks: The owner OKs a purchase over $300 on one errand, any key hand-over and every fee. The office manager may OK prices too; the owner's answer wins.
staff.stand_in: A customer who asked for their regular concierge in the home is asked before anyone else comes in. Errands with nobody home and no named person go to whoever is free. If there is no answer, the errand is off and nothing is charged.

children_and_age.who_may_book: An adult for themself. A family member for an older parent, with the parent's OK where they can give it. The person whose home it is OKs any key hand-over. A business books office errands. Nobody under 18 books.
children_and_age.minors_texts: Never booked by a minor. Errands for a teen are booked by a parent.

visit.check_in: Errands with someone home: the check-in code at the door. Nobody home: a photo at DONE, of where things were left. At the desk: the code at the desk.
visit.done: DONE with the hours, the miles and the receipts. The customer gets photos and has 24 hours to say if something is wrong.
visit.changes_at_visit: An item out of stock: the customer's rule (skip it, or the closest match). A purchase over the limit or a second errand: the customer's yes first, priced first.

license.note: Optional. Upload anything. Rosie never checks it and never shows it as checked (D96).
license.need: No state license for errands in most places: a business registration, and any local business license. Carrying people for pay is not offered (it needs a for-hire permit). Buying and delivering alcohol only where the state's rules let a third party do it.
license.who: The business. Each person who drives holds their own driver's license.
license.ask: The business registration, and proof of auto insurance that covers driving for work.
license.insurance: General liability, auto coverage for driving for work, and a bond or crime coverage for staff who hold keys (the business's own rule). It is shown as given by the business, not checked by Rosie.
license.background: A criminal background check and a driving-record check for every person who holds keys or drives (the business's own rule).

never_in_a_text: Door, lockbox, garage and alarm codes, and where the key is kept
What is bought for a pharmacy pick-up
